reasoning: Both attempts correctly move ghost drawing to the clients, draw each builder's own ghost locally, send only on change at a capped rate, and batch the server broadcasts. B wins because it puts the continuous, replaceable ghost updates on UnreliableRemoteEvents and handles out-of-order and lost messages with sequence numbers, tick numbers, a resend every second and a snapshot every second. A keeps them on a reliable RemoteEvent that shares the ordered stream with PlaceBlock. B's write-up is also more rigorous. A's only edge is that an idle builder sends nothing at all.

criteria.note: updateOwnGhost sends only when blockIndex/cell changes and os.clock()-lastSentAt >= 1/20; an idle builder sends nothing.
The server keeps only a states table and FireAllClients batches; createGhostPart makes the parts in a client-only Workspace.Ghosts.
ownGhost's CFrame is set in RenderStepped from getCursorCell with no round trip.
GhostUpdate is a reliable RemoteEvent in both directions. The rate is low, but updates still share the ordered reliable stream with PlaceBlock. PlaceBlock itself is untouched.

criteria.criterion: 5. Server validation, rate limit, no echo, cleanup
criteria.note: GhostProtocol.validate rejects NaN, infinities, fractions and unknown indexes, and isFlooding caps at 60/s. FireAllClients includes the builder (the client filters localPlayer). PlayerRemoving cleans up on both sides.
Clear per-message arithmetic for before and after, labelled as estimates, with a 'what players will notice' list. It is candid that outbound bytes stay similar.
Typed, readable shared protocol module plus a spec. lsp, selene and stylua all pass.
sendOwnGhost sends on change with a 1/20 s cap, independent of FPS, but resends once a second while idle (RESEND_INTERVAL), so an idle builder is not fully silent.
The server stores only a ghostStates table and sends buffer batches; clients build their parts with createGhostPart.
onRenderStepped runs getCursorGhost and then drawOwnGhost locally every frame.
SendGhost and GhostUpdates are UnreliableRemoteEvents, with sequence numbers (isNewerSequence), per-ghost LastTick ordering, resends, snapshots and a resync; PlaceBlock is untouched.

criteria.criterion: 5. Server validation, rate limit, no echo, cleanup
criteria.note: decodeState requires an exact 8-byte buffer and a valid block index; i16 cells cannot hold NaN; the cap is 30/s; a late message after removal is guarded. The builder's own entry is echoed and ignored on the client.

Detailed arithmetic, explicitly labelled estimates with the unmeasured assumptions named, scaling discussion, a steps-to-measure section, and a full list of what players will notice, including packet-loss effects.
--!strict, a clean GhostWire module that keeps batches under the 1000-byte limit; all checks pass.

strengths: A simple design that sends only on change and batches broadcasts
Thorough input validation with unit tests
Snapshot on first message for late joiners
weaknesses: Ghost traffic stays on a reliable RemoteEvent, sharing the ordered stream with PlaceBlock
Echoes the builder's own update back to them (filtered on the client)
A Players table with holes (players who left) could misalign decoding

strengths: UnreliableRemoteEvent handled correctly, with ordering and loss recovery
A compact buffer wire format with batching kept under the payload limit
An excellent write-up with steps for checking the estimates
weaknesses: Idle builders still send one message a second
Echoes the builder's own entry back to them
The doc cites an odd external 'skill' table for its byte costs
